verdict.rationale: Zulip documents a first-party bot framework for writing and running custom bots, plus the Zulip Botserver for deploying them. It also maintains a machine-readable OpenAPI spec and an API feature-level changelog meant for building clients that work across server versions. That is real first-party tooling to build against, but the pack never names an official client SDK library or its languages, so SDK support is only implied. missing for 10: explicitly documented official SDK libraries (e.g., named Python/JS client packages), language coverage, SDK reference docs, independent corroboration of SDK use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Zulip’s API has a powerful framework for interactive bots that react to messages in Zulip. You can write and run a custom bot, or run an existing Zulip bot.
deploying it on a server using the Zulip Botserver
The API feature levels system used in this changelog is designed to make it possible to write API clients... that work with a wide range of server versions
